fields.title: Product vision
fields.heading: ## Product vision
fields.excerpt:
## Product vision

**Status:** owner-authored direction from the initial brief; not representative-user evidence or implementation approval.

Make structured engineering information as easy to create, connect and edit as a spreadsheet, with typed relationships, traceability, history and meaningful change context. The owner's experience of navigation and process overhead in enterprise requirements tools motivates this hypothesis.

Use one domain-independent model for humans and agents. Begin locally with a project database, minimal setup and no cloud account. Deeper traceability and team use should grow from the same semantics without complicating ordinary authoring. Shared servers, PostgreSQL, permissions and broad collaboration remain future work.

The original need IDs remain stable:

### UN-001 — Organize structured information

Configure familiar information types—requirements, designs, components, tests, risks, decisions, tasks, experiments and evidence—without changing Tracer's source. Templates are optional; a task tracker should not require requirements-management vocabulary.

### UN-002 — Connect information

Create typed, directed relationships with their own identity, fields and history. Navigate in either direction across hierarchies, shared contributions and cross-domain networks without forcing a tree.

### UN-003 — Understand completeness and impact

Find gaps and possible change consequences under explicit project expectations. Reachability, structural completeness, assessed impact and successful execution are distinct; links and coverage counts do not establish satisfaction or readiness.

### UN-004 — Track changes and preserve history

Explain what changed, when, why and by whom, including relationships. Reconstruct reproducible baselines and compare logical states through semantic and deterministic textual differences. Full export/diff/restoration workflows remain undelivered.

### UN-005 — Work through the most appropriate interface

Use tables, graphs, matrices or document-like views over the same information, validation and history. The selected map experience is shared across examples. This goal does not imply every view currently supports every edit.

### Scope, generality and limits

Medical devices, software, aerospace, manufacturing/quality, research and regulatory evidence use the same primitives and may coexist in one project. Optional schemas express vocabulary and policy; they neither establish compliance nor impose universal approval stages. See [industry workflows](industry-workflows/README.md).

Start with a useful local engineering foundation. Enterprise requirements-tool parity, PLM/ERP, specialized compliance, distributed storage, comprehensive workflow automation and an elaborate plugin ecosystem are outside initial scope. Add infrastructure when its value is demonstrated.

[Vision scenarios](user-journeys.md#vision-scenarios-and-remaining-proof) make the ambition testable; [validation milestones](development-flow.md#validation-milestones) define the required evidence.

fields.title: 5. Small readiness/completion decisions
fields.heading: ## 5. Small readiness/completion decisions
fields.excerpt:
## 5. Small readiness/completion decisions

- **Ready to implement:** selected task/concept, bounded scope, sufficient evidence, failure handling, checks and validation plan. Experiment on risky unknowns.
- **Implemented/verified:** agreed behavior passes checks; candidate and limits are reviewable.
- **Validated:** representative task evidence supports a stated use/context. Owner walkthroughs remain provisional.
- **Release-ready:** appropriate usefulness, correctness and operational evidence, resolved critical dependencies and explicit authority.

After sustaining changes, reassess affected specs, checks and scenarios. Retain passing evidence where its coverage remains applicable.

fields.title: Current limits
fields.heading: ## Current limits
fields.excerpt:
## Current limits

- The production map reads a transactional native snapshot bounded to 10,000 artifacts and 100,000 relationships. Drawing/query bounds are disclosed separately.
- The workbench draws up to 50 artifacts and projects up to 500 trace rows or 100 terminal links per grouped cell. It is not virtualized.
- Assessment discovery follows declared input/captured-output scope, five evaluations per page. Ordinary graph connectivity is not an assessed dependency or proof of impact.
- Unsaved drafts remain tab-local and are deliberately excluded from recovery. Leaving/reloading warns; uncertain writes restore a pause without replay. Spatial and investigation recovery uses browser local storage, keyed by project identity and tied to the same browser/origin. Saved engineering records, review decisions and named Matrix path recipes persist in SQLite.
- Spreadsheet paste/bulk mutation, portable workspace context and arbitrary two-revision comparison remain open. Matrix saved recipes currently support outgoing path columns; receipt creation pickers remain bounded to 1,000 items.
- PostgreSQL parity, authenticated collaboration, hosted integrations, restoration and standalone packaging remain future work.

fields.title: Open work
fields.heading: ## Open work
fields.excerpt:
## Open work

Evaluate complete create → connect → modify → investigate → assess tasks with representative users in more than one domain. An unfamiliar-user session has not been run. Use observed next-action choices, completion time, assistance, errors and context loss to prioritize larger-dataset interaction, clearer review context and remaining authoring friction. Automated checks and visual consistency are supporting evidence, not substitutes for task validation.

fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-01 — Start from recognizable engineering work

fields.title: Author and revise coherent design information
fields.statement: Express intent with surrounding rationale, revise related items and distinguish drafts from established information. **Basis:** UR-2/4/14; VI-1. Investigate statement length, cell/batch versus long-form work, attributes and review states. Preserve existing software source artifacts; compulsory grammar and per-item editors are unproven.
fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-02 — Author and revise coherent design information

fields.title: Understand and manipulate relationships across levels
fields.statement: Work with parents, children, siblings and cross-cutting relationships together; explain contributions, navigate whole/detail and recognize shared identity. **Basis:** UR-1/2/4/7/14; VI-1. Investigate direction, multiple parents, link attributes, dense branches and branch-level actions. Software may connect needs, modules and tests without successive requirement levels; no strict tree is required. The Jama criticism is owner experience, not a claim about every version.
fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-03 — Understand and manipulate relationships across levels

fields.title: Identify meaningful completeness gaps and next work
fields.statement: Explain an unresolved obligation under declared project expectations and choose the next action. **Basis:** UR-4/15; VI-1. An approved requirement lacking an implementation link is a candidate gap: code may exist but be unlinked. Planned, partial, outdated and current realization must remain distinguishable, including relevant requirement/version scope. Approval, implementation coverage, test coverage and execution results are separate. Investigate applicability and priority; automatic scheduling/ownership remain HY.
fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-04 — Identify meaningful completeness gaps and next work

fields.title: Understand a proposed change before committing it
fields.statement: Start from one modification/removal, compare intent and see candidate consequences with recorded paths or stated reasoning. Retain system requirements whether preserved or explicitly revised. **Basis:** UR-4/6/11/14; VI-1. Motor/load/timing examples are user reports without supplied design/test artifacts. Investigate proposal staging, review, removal, old evidence and unaffected links; no impact algorithm or approval workflow is selected. Missing paths cannot prove no impact.

fields.title: Track important quantitative meaning without forcing formalization
fields.statement: Explain limits, allocations and derivations while preserving prose and judgment. Avoid coupling identical numbers or silently rewriting children. **Basis:** UR-5; structured parameters/computation are HY; no real quantitative artifact yet. Investigate references, inheritance, budgets, formulas, independent choices, units, overhead, uncertainty and conditions. Formula editing and extraction are not requirements.
fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-06 — Track important quantitative meaning without forcing formalization

fields.title: Judge evidence and record a defensible decision
fields.statement: Inspect relevant inputs/evidence, understand changed or unknown conditions and retain reasoning. **Basis:** VI-1, existing evidence semantics, UR-14; detailed reviewer tasks are HY. Investigate review packages, comparisons, handoffs and authority. A test file, code link and revision-specific result are separate facts; none alone proves need satisfaction. fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-09 — Keep orientation while changing working level or representation

fields.title: begin without an extensive setup detour
fields.statement:
### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour

> As an author starting a design, I want to work with recognizable information so I can begin expressing the design instead of learning the tool's internal model.

**Needs:** PN-01, PN-02. **Basis:** vision plus hypothesis; preferred onboarding method unknown.

**Candidate acceptance:** users recognize the available information and what is missing; they can start one meaningful item without first constructing a complete project ontology. Existing data brought into the project is not silently lost or falsely represented as validated.

**Investigate:** write from scratch, paste/import or start from a template? Prototype these alternatives rather than implementing all three now.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour

fields.title: author in context and move between levels
fields.statement:
### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels

> As an author, I want to inspect the relevant parent intent while writing a child requirement so I can explain how the child contributes without repeatedly reconstructing context.

**Needs:** PN-02, PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1, UR-2, UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** free text is usable without compulsory formal syntax; an item can relate to an existing parent or remain explicitly unlinked; applicable field/relationship actions are reachable in the working context; changing scope does not silently lose the draft.

**Exceptions:** long statements, optional attributes, multiple parents, uncertain relationships and a parent that changed while drafting.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels

fields.title: inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.statement:
### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity

> As an engineer reviewing decomposition, I want to see the other items contributing under the relevant parent so I can judge the family together rather than inspect isolated statements.

**Needs:** PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1.

**Candidate acceptance:** the parent and relationship defining the family are explainable; shared children remain recognizable as the same underlying item; editing one identity does not create divergence among its appearances; users can return to the wider scope with drafts intact.

**Exceptions:** a child belongs to two parents, appears along several paths, or has different kinds of sibling relationships. Test whether the user wants immediate siblings or the whole branch; do not assume they are equivalent.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity

fields.title: resolve one meaningful completeness gap
fields.statement:
### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap

> As an engineer building a design, I want to know which obligation is unresolved and why so I can choose the next appropriate work.

**Needs:** PN-04, PN-03, PN-07. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-15; exact scope/policies are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** a displayed gap has an explainable expectation and scope; the user can inspect existing candidates before creating duplicate information; an appropriate new connection resolves that structural gap without falsely declaring the design/evidence valid; other unresolved obligations remain visible.

**Software acceptance example (UR-15):** where the project marks a requirement approved, see whether an actual implementation artifact is linked. With no such link, show implementation as not traced and likely outstanding; offer the task choices of implementing it, linking existing code or investigating uncertainty. Do not force a new implementation when the code already exists. A link to a planned task/design is not an actual-code realization link; partial or outdated mappings retain their unresolved scope. Adding an appropriate link closes the trace gap, not automatically the implementation/verification judgment.

**Exceptions:** an item is intentionally not applicable, the expectation is unknown, existing implementation is unlinked, a link covers only part of the requirement or refers to older behavior, or old evidence uses different inputs. Represent uncertainty rather than inventing a complete/incomplete judgment.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap

fields.title: see impact before accepting a change
fields.statement:
### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change

> As an engineer proposing a modification, I want to compare it with the established state and inspect explainable consequences so I can review the proposal before changing the authoritative design.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-6, UR-11; specific staging mechanisms are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** proposed versus committed information is distinguishable; impact candidates show the paths/reasons that make them relevant; browsing does not write changes; connection alone is not presented as proof that the connected item must change; unmodeled consequences remain explicitly possible.

**Exceptions:** cyclic or dense networks, shared children, changed schema, missing/deleted items and incomplete source knowledge. A bounded result must explain its scope, not imply a complete impact census.
fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change

fields.title: reason about removal
fields.statement:
### SC-02 — reason about removal

> As an engineer considering removing information, I want to see what relies on it so I can decide how to address those obligations without losing the established history.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** removing, filtering out, disconnecting and superseding are distinguishable; references and unresolved obligations are explained; no silent cascade; established history remains inspectable; users know whether anything was committed.

**Investigate:** actual review/approval authority and the semantics of retirement versus deletion. Do not introduce automatic cascade or organizational approval merely because it would simplify a mockup.
fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-02 — reason about removal

fields.title: reassess evidence without rewriting its past
fields.statement:
### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past

> As a reviewer, I want to inspect changed inputs and the original evidence so I can record why the evidence does or does not support the decision now.

**Needs:** PN-07, PN-05, PN-08. **Basis:** vision/existing evidence model; detailed reviewer task is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** coverage, freshness, uncertainty and review decision remain separate; original snapshots/rationale remain accessible; the comparison used while drafting is identifiable; a relevant intervening change requires an explicit new assessment rather than silent token adoption; acceptance does not erase drift.

**Exceptions:** missing observations, unrelated edits, relevant later changes, superseded evidence and conflicting reviewer assumptions. Local provenance labels are not authenticated approval authority.
fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past

fields.title: quantitative meaning without overconstraint
fields.statement:
## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint

> As an engineer changing an important specification, I want to understand where the value comes from and where it is used so I can assess the consequences without forcing every requirement into a formal model.

**Needs:** PN-06, PN-02, PN-05. **Basis:** UR-5; representation and computation are HY.

**Toy scenario:** an overall timing limit is 100 ms, with explicitly declared 60 ms and 40 ms allocations. Propose changing the total to 80 ms. These are not medical specifications. Any arithmetic requires explicit combination and overhead assumptions.

**Candidate acceptance examples:**

- Free-text-only requirements remain authorable and reviewable.
- If a value is deliberately shared, its confirmed consumers are identifiable; an unrelated identical number is not automatically coupled.
- An explicitly modeled calculation may report a result/violation under its declared assumptions, with units and explanation.
- A parent limit change exposes the allocation question but does not silently proportionally scale or rewrite children.
- A child allocation change can raise a feasibility question for the parent without rewriting the parent's intent.
- Missing derivation knowledge is not represented as a satisfied constraint or no impact.
- Declared constraints, possible engineering impact and review decisions are distinguishable.

**Alternatives to test:** ordinary prose with annotated values, optional named typed values, linked value references, and human-authored derivation explanations. A general formula language or extraction engine is not assumed.

**Additional cases:** inconsistent units, rounding, tolerances, ranges, conditions, repeated values, independent choices and removal of a referenced value. Replace the toy example with one real artifact before specifying storage or arithmetic behavior.
fields.sourceHeading: ## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint

fields.title: resume and recover safely
fields.statement:
## 5. Cross-cutting story R-01 — resume and recover safely

> As an engineer interrupted during work, I want to retain my proposal and orientation so I can resume or reconcile it without losing information or overwriting someone else's change.

**Needs:** PN-08, PN-09. **Basis:** vision; preferred saving/recovery model is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** context/selection and save status are understandable; switching level or representation does not silently discard drafts; a failed read cannot authorize editing stale information as if current; object/schema conflicts preserve the attempt; historical inspection does not masquerade as editing current state.

**Investigate:** autosave versus explicit save, reopening after shutdown, undo, and what should be retained across sessions. Prototype and actual repository safety capabilities may differ; label unsupported recovery behavior honestly.
fields.sourceHeading: ## 5. Cross-cutting story R-01 — resume and recover safely

## Native application

Normal launch opens `ui/workbench/` Graph / Matrix / History over the selected database. Orbit, Aster and empty projects share this UI/core. Project tools retains full item/link editing, model configuration, receipt authoring, configurations, documentation and the Development map.

SQLite supports version-guarded atomic writes, immutable history, directed links, saved views, exact configurations, baselines, structural coverage and scoped change investigation. Captured inputs, current freshness and review decisions remain separate.

fields.title: Inspector and contextual editing polish
fields.heading: ## Inspector and contextual editing polish
fields.excerpt:
## Inspector and contextual editing polish

2026-10-17: text editors expose actual draft state, keyboard save/cancel and saving locks. Focus returns to the edited control; resize retains caret, and artifact/relationship reading positions survive rerenders and Graph/Matrix/History returns. Unchanged optional fields remain absent and clean editors do not warn on reload. Saving or cancelling one field retains other unsaved values; only a confirmed save advances the captured version, using its own returned version even if another actor edits before refresh. Readers offer explicit resume/discard actions. Drafts and reading positions stay tab-local.

Relationship creation now searches compatible targets by identifier or title with bounded keyboard-operable suggestions and exact key selection, readable source/target context, scope requirements and explicit Cancel. Relationship inspection returns directly to the artifact and its connection control, remains usable in narrow sheets and offers scope editing only for declared text fields. Unchanged scope saves add no revision. Existing version/schema/endpoint guards, unknown-save inspection and native write paths remain authoritative.

Focused checks cover 1440px/680px/390px (844px phone height), retained drafts/partial saves, independent reading positions, caret/focus, no-op revisions, clean reload, compatible title search, exact target selection and pending-save cancellation/duplicate prevention. Desktop and phone screenshots were inspected. The final `npm run check` passed formatting, strict types, lint, 408 unit tests, 165 browser tests, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and dependency/duplication/complexity gates. Additional cases cover intervening edits between save and refresh, and locked connection proposals during pending writes. No quality limits or exclusions changed. The fresh-user task script is recorded in the UX plan; no unfamiliar participant session has been run, so these checks establish browser behavior rather than usability validation.

fields.title: Integrated workflow
fields.heading: ## Integrated workflow
fields.excerpt:
## Integrated workflow

`npm start`/demo use production sources; `npm run workbench` launches disposable Aster/Gatherline review databases. The [review guide](ux-artifacts/product-identity/README.md) owns regression orchestration. Studies re-export production modules; production cannot import studies.

Implemented workflows include:

- Create artifacts from a title-first Matrix row, revealing schema-required fields before commit.
- Link compatible existing artifacts or atomically create an artifact and its connection.
- Edit fields in floating editors while preserving table geometry, scroll and canonical shared identity.
- Retain artifact, relationship, revision and investigation scope across Graph, Matrix and History.
- Explore recorded dependency paths with stable positions, readable fitted titles and contextual actions.
- Author an ordinary evaluation receipt with exact input items/fields or historical pins, then compare captured/current inputs and record an immutable assessment with rationale. No fixture preparation is required for ordinary authoring.
- Save named Matrix row/path/search recipes in SQLite; recover graph positions, view settings, selected revision and investigation scope in the same browser/origin after reload.
- Preserve drafts across view changes, reject stale versions/tokens and inspect uncertain saves without automatic replay.
- Use a docked inspector, drawer or compact/partial sheet according to available workspace; historical states are read-only.

The fresh-project browser journey defines a small custom model, creates and connects two records, authors a selected-field receipt, changes the captured statement, investigates its exact link, records Needs reevaluation, saves a Matrix recipe and reloads the same decision, investigation and graph positions. It passes at 1440px and 680px.

The established Aster assessment scenario modifies PRS-02 from 10–40°C to 5–45°C at r400, retains twenty exact recorded links across views, identifies changed captured inputs, records Needs reevaluation and reloads the same decision. The receipt and native project revision remain unchanged by the review. All example outcomes are explicitly simulated.

fields.acceptance: Each queue has complete bounded counts and direct actions; missing configuration or read failure cannot appear as zero work.
fields.remaining: Assignment, linked follow-ups, closure criteria and user validation remain separate.

fields.title: Separate next-work queues
fields.heading: ## Separate next-work queues
fields.excerpt:
## Separate next-work queues

2026-10-17: [UR-62](user-needs.md) adds **Next work** in the shared workspace header and Project tools, plus `Tracer.getNextWork`, CLI `next-work get` and typed `GET /api/next-work`. Missing statements, unallocated requirements, missing verification plans, changed evidence inputs and unresolved reviews have independent counts, explanations and direct existing edit/review actions. Each complete bounded snapshot retains native/model/evidence context; local ten-row paging never truncates counts. Missing configuration and failed reads cannot masquerade as zero work.

Engineering starter policies supply compatible defaults. Custom models choose declared type/text-field and saved policy roles explicitly, without model changes; resetting defaults recovers from removed policies. Structural queues identify zero qualifying targets under complete directional/population rules, leaving other minimum-count deficits in Coverage. Evidence reuses declared-input comparison and review applicability. Confirmed drift, unknown inputs, outcomes and judgments remain separate; Accepted/Acknowledged resolves review work only, Needs reevaluation remains open and explicitly superseded results leave current work queues.

Hidden editors/reviews retain drafts, conflicting selection preserves their owners, and returning refreshes queues. Fresh record/comparison reads retain schema/version/token guards and uncertain-write pauses. No migration, observation, new task store or alternate write path is introduced. The [next-work guide](next-work.md) owns full membership rules, configuration, engineering budgets and interface formats; linked follow-up work remains separate scope.

Focused verification passed eight unit/integration cases and five browser journeys at 1440/680/390px. Cases cover queue independence, complete paging, policy filters/directions, selected-field drift, unknowns, retired reviews, supersession, read/budget errors, snapshot isolation, CLI/HTTP parity/project selection, edits/connections/review decisions, retained drafts, reload and custom-model recovery. Screenshots were inspected at all three widths and 153 local file links resolved. The final `npm run check` passed formatting, strict types, lint, 404 unit tests, 152 browser tests, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and dependency/duplication/complexity gates. Queue refresh/draft ownership and rendering were split into cohesive components to meet the existing complexity limits. No quality limits, baselines or exclusions changed.

fields.heading: ## Practical CSV import

## Practical CSV import

2026-10-17: [UR-60](user-needs.md) adds **Project tools → Import CSV** with file/paste input, schema-aware column mapping, optional outgoing links and a separate existing-record link mode. Exact case-sensitive active keys resolve existing records and later rows in the same file. Duplicate keys/connections, malformed rows, missing targets, invalid endpoints and required/typed cell errors block the entire import; ignored columns are explicit. Preview rows/errors page locally without truncating validation. CSV drafts remain tab-local.

The portable parser/planner exports feed the existing guarded changeset route; there is no staging store, alternate write path or storage migration. Explicit create IDs, model/endpoint captures and duplicate-link guards preserve native validation and unknown-outcome inspection. Optional native changeset `expectedProjectRevision` is checked inside the transaction before writes; CSV commits supply the exact preview head, so any intervening native change requires a new preview. Preview also rejects files whose resulting counts would exceed the shared complete-workspace bounds. Confirmed saves identify one revision and clear the draft; failed/uncertain saves retain data/mapping without replay or partial records/history.

The final `npm run check` passed formatting, strict types, lint, 391 unit tests, 144 browser tests, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and dependency/duplication/complexity gates. Eleven CSV unit cases cover quoting/physical lines, typed values, forward/existing keys, duplicate and missing links, mapping/batch/byte/population limits, captured-head checks, stale endpoints/schema and full rollback. Four browser journeys cover desktop/680px mapping/error/commit/read-back/reload, stale-preview rejection and lost-response locking. Additional browser checks verified malformed UTF-8/CSV, complete error/row pagination and successful link-only import with metadata. Preview/error screenshots were inspected at both widths; 140 local file/heading links resolved. The full run also caught and corrected the retained desk-light journey's old documentation path; it now reads the customization guide. No quality limits or exclusions changed.

One file imports one record type or one relationship type; record mode can add up to eight outgoing key-column link mappings. Existing records are never overwritten. Workbook parsing, updates/merges, saved mapping recipes, multi-key cells and evidence/file import remain outside this slice. The [CSV import guide](csv-import.md) owns formats, bounds and the reusable script workflow.

## Deterministic project export

2026-10-17: [UR-61](user-needs.md) adds **Project tools → Export project**, `project export` CLI and typed `GET /api/project-export` through `Tracer.exportProject()` and the shared canonical serializer. One transaction captures current schema/records/links, all recorded native changesets/revisions (including tombstones), immutable evidence/configurations/baselines and current saved views. Exact native versions, historical schemas, original actor/reason/time, captured paths/pins, external observations and review decisions remain unchanged. Evidence/capture boundaries stay separate from native revision; external content is referenced rather than read or bundled.

Unchanged stored content produces identical UTF-8 JSON bytes across interfaces and restarts. Prepared browser bytes remain fixed after later changes; re-preparation explicitly adopts new content, while a failed preparation clears the download. Exhaustive paging is independent of rendering bounds and rejects beyond 250,000 entries / 64 MiB without a partial response. The [export guide](project-export.md) owns format, ordering, preservation instructions and budgets. Selected-baseline packages and restore remain separate scope.

Focused verification passed five unit/integration cases and three browser journeys at 1440/680px, covering byte parity/restart, historical/deleted inputs, unknown/observed external references, every collection's pagination, queued writes, read/capacity failures, fixed downloads, retry and malformed-response rejection. The final `npm run check` passed formatting, strict types, lint, 396 unit tests, 147 browser tests, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and dependency/duplication/complexity gates. The serializer also rejects non-JSON values; its focused cases passed after that final guard was added. ## Persistent Engineering starter

2026-10-17: the fresh-project slice adds optional acceptance criteria, verification methods/expected results and subsystem/build text references to the Engineering starter. Four explicit structural policies distinguish intent trace, design allocation, requirement-to-plan mapping and design-under-test mapping. Basic mappings no longer require review/version metadata. Existing stored models remain authoritative and are not upgraded on reopen.

First model save optionally installs three named outgoing Matrix recipes in the same transaction as schema/coverage. Invalid or duplicate paths roll back all setup, and stale/repeated setup cannot duplicate recipes. Empty configured projects enter the longest supported saved trace and offer New requirement. Model/create/item dirty reporting clears confirmed forms. The launcher prints an exact, quoted resume command preserving database, guides, companion project and port.

Added three setup contract cases and desktop/680px journeys: UI-save the starter, reload without false unsaved warnings, author a plan with method/expected result/build, create/link a requirement and design, save acceptance, restart the server and load the same recipe in a clean browser. Unit tests also distinguish direct requirement-plan coverage from design-to-test reachability and verify rollback, customization and database reopen. The additional method/expected-result/build read-back checks pass at both widths. Setup and trace screenshots were inspected at desktop and 680px, including dialog overflow. A launcher smoke check verified the resume command with quoted database paths and the actual origin port. The [Engineering walkthrough](getting-started.md#start-your-own-project) documents starting and resuming real work with a stable database file.

fields.title: Shared API and first-class headless HTTP
fields.heading: ## Shared API and first-class headless HTTP
fields.excerpt:
## Shared API and first-class headless HTTP

2026-10-18: extracted typed API dispatch from local HTTP/static hosting. Exhaustive handler, request-decoder and query-codec tables follow the wire contract; application services retain semantic validation and transaction ownership. Shared query codecs fix the impact relationship-type array mismatch. Strict request objects reject unsupported fields, including actor/provenance injection; schema/session reads now reject query parameters. Shared error codes feed client decoding and exhaustive HTTP status mapping.

Added the separate `@tracer-local/core/client` source entry point and routed browser adapters through it without bypassing the mutation controller. Each client fixes its server/project/header configuration, owns its session, captures read queries, accepts fetch injection/cancellation and never automatically retries writes. `@tracer-local/core/server` exposes a loopback headless host with trusted process provenance and allowlisted projects. `npm run serve:api -- --db PATH` starts without frontend assets/builds and prints a headless resume command.

Integration checks exercise real client/server edits, conflicts, provenance, evidence/reviews/captures/views/export, project/server/session isolation, query-codec round trips, malformed input/response handling and caller-mutated queries. A committed write whose response is lost yields `outcome_unknown` and one saved record. A separate launcher smoke test runs outside the checkout without `dist`, writes through the client and confirms no static pages are served. Readiness for organizational hosting and PostgreSQL parity remain separate future work. The architecture and developer reference own the contracts, usage and recovery guidance.

Strict validation exposed the shared object editor sending stored relationship `id`/`version` metadata inside an update's `input`. It now constructs the declared type/source/target/fields payload, keeping identity/version guards at operation level. Route-specific guards also replace a branching query guard without changing rejection behavior or quality limits.

Verification passed: 433 unit tests, 178 browser tests on the corrected editor, all workbench journeys, production/harness builds, strict types, lint, formatting and merged-coverage dependency/duplication/complexity gates. Focused final-source API/launcher/contract/transport checks also passed (21 tests), refreshing coverage after module moves. No quality thresholds or exclusions changed.

fields.title: Durable changeset command recovery
fields.heading: ## Durable changeset command recovery
fields.excerpt:
## Durable changeset command recovery

2026-10-18: added optional project-scoped `commandId` to changeset input and `Tracer.getChangesetOutcome`, with shared HTTP/client and CLI access. Commands retain invocation-time input/provenance, compare canonical intent before current-state guards, and return the original committed result for an exact repeat. Different content, guards, operation order or trusted provenance under a successful identity conflict. Unidentified calls preserve their existing behavior. Result types moved to core with their public application re-exports retained.

Application-owned transaction operations persist successful outcomes atomically with native state, history and revision allocation. SQLite physical format 9 adds immutable outcomes with unique command/changeset identities; older-format migrations preserve existing data/history. Rejections and rollbacks reserve no command ID. Outcomes survive restart and later edits/deletion/schema changes. A missing lookup does not prove an in-flight command failed. There is no automatic retry or expiry, and other mutation types remain outside this changeset-only ledger. The database backup preserves operational outcomes; project JSON export excludes them. Architecture and developer guidance own contracts and recovery examples.

Regression checks cover commit → lost response → server/repository restart → exact lookup/repeat without duplication, concurrent same/different intent, project isolation, cross-connection contention and explicit recovery, full rollback after inserting an outcome, ordered intermediate results/tombstones, invocation capture and CLI recovery across processes. Existing migration fixtures now remove the new table when reconstructing older formats and reject the next unsupported format.

Verification passed: 446 unit tests, strict types, lint, formatting, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and final merged-coverage dependency/duplication/complexity gates. The full browser run passed 177 of 178 scenarios; the remaining narrow CSV scenario timed out waiting for its initial Project tools button before any mutation. All four CSV scenarios passed an isolated rerun, including that case. No source workaround, quality threshold or exclusion changed.

fields.title: API capability discovery and generated reference
fields.heading: ## API capability discovery and generated reference
fields.excerpt:
## API capability discovery and generated reference

2026-10-19: added typed `GET /api/capabilities` with independent `tracer-http` contract version 1, registry-derived operations/features and limits shared with changeset/HTTP enforcement. Discovery needs no model or storage transaction and preserves origin/project/no-cache guards. The first feature promise is `changeset-command-recovery`. Additive operations/features/response fields retain contract 1; incompatible wire or behavior changes require a new contract version.

Clients can opt into captured `require` settings on construction or call `checkCompatibility` explicitly. Checks verify identity, exact supported version, features, operations and minimum limits before writes; configured clients check before obtaining a session. Pending/failed checks block new writes, stale checks cannot restore readiness, and explicit requirements cannot weaken configured ones. Legacy discovery absence reports client-only `incompatible_api`; invalid/unavailable/cancelled reads retain their read/server errors. Existing clients keep their connection behavior until opting in. No automatic retries or per-write negotiation were added.

Query codecs and write helpers expose request metadata used by `npm run api:reference` to generate `docs/api-reference.md`. The unit suite rejects reference drift. This is an endpoint/request index; nested types and semantic guards retain their existing owners. The architecture and developer reference document usage, version policy, scope and recovery.

Verification passed: 455 unit tests, strict types, lint, formatting, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and final merged-coverage dependency/duplication/complexity gates. New checks cover empty/model-changed discovery without storage reads, origin/project guards, actual advertised-limit enforcement, incompatible/missing/malformed discovery with zero POSTs, captured requirements, additive extensions and stale-check ordering. After removing duplicate capability type declarations, 18 focused API tests passed against the final source. The full browser run passed 177 of 178 scenarios; the remaining Engineering setup case timed out waiting for the Matrix button after reopening the server. Both desktop/narrow setup cases passed an isolated rerun. No source workaround, quality threshold or exclusion changed.

fields.title: ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour
fields.heading: ### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour
fields.excerpt:
### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour

> As an author starting a design, I want to work with recognizable information so I can begin expressing the design instead of learning the tool's internal model.

**Needs:** PN-01, PN-02. **Basis:** vision plus hypothesis; preferred onboarding method unknown.

**Candidate acceptance:** users recognize the available information and what is missing; they can start one meaningful item without first constructing a complete project ontology. Existing data brought into the project is not silently lost or falsely represented as validated.

**Investigate:** write from scratch, paste/import or start from a template? Prototype these alternatives rather than implementing all three now.

fields.title: ND-02 — author in context and move between levels
fields.heading: ### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels
fields.excerpt:
### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels

> As an author, I want to inspect the relevant parent intent while writing a child requirement so I can explain how the child contributes without repeatedly reconstructing context.

**Needs:** PN-02, PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1, UR-2, UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** free text is usable without compulsory formal syntax; an item can relate to an existing parent or remain explicitly unlinked; applicable field/relationship actions are reachable in the working context; changing scope does not silently lose the draft.

**Exceptions:** long statements, optional attributes, multiple parents, uncertain relationships and a parent that changed while drafting.

fields.title: ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.heading: ### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.excerpt:
### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity

> As an engineer reviewing decomposition, I want to see the other items contributing under the relevant parent so I can judge the family together rather than inspect isolated statements.

**Needs:** PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1.

**Candidate acceptance:** the parent and relationship defining the family are explainable; shared children remain recognizable as the same underlying item; editing one identity does not create divergence among its appearances; users can return to the wider scope with drafts intact.

**Exceptions:** a child belongs to two parents, appears along several paths, or has different kinds of sibling relationships. Test whether the user wants immediate siblings or the whole branch; do not assume they are equivalent.

fields.title: ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap
fields.heading: ### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap
fields.excerpt:
### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap

> As an engineer building a design, I want to know which obligation is unresolved and why so I can choose the next appropriate work.

**Needs:** PN-04, PN-03, PN-07. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-15; exact scope/policies are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** a displayed gap has an explainable expectation and scope; the user can inspect existing candidates before creating duplicate information; an appropriate new connection resolves that structural gap without falsely declaring the design/evidence valid; other unresolved obligations remain visible.

**Software acceptance example (UR-15):** where the project marks a requirement approved, see whether an actual implementation artifact is linked. With no such link, show implementation as not traced and likely outstanding; offer the task choices of implementing it, linking existing code or investigating uncertainty. Do not force a new implementation when the code already exists. A link to a planned task/design is not an actual-code realization link; partial or outdated mappings retain their unresolved scope. Adding an appropriate link closes the trace gap, not automatically the implementation/verification judgment.

**Exceptions:** an item is intentionally not applicable, the expectation is unknown, existing implementation is unlinked, a link covers only part of the requirement or refers to older behavior, or old evidence uses different inputs. Represent uncertainty rather than inventing a complete/incomplete judgment.

fields.title: SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change
fields.heading: ### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change

### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change

> As an engineer proposing a modification, I want to compare it with the established state and inspect explainable consequences so I can review the proposal before changing the authoritative design.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-6, UR-11; specific staging mechanisms are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** proposed versus committed information is distinguishable; impact candidates show the paths/reasons that make them relevant; browsing does not write changes; connection alone is not presented as proof that the connected item must change; unmodeled consequences remain explicitly possible.

**Exceptions:** cyclic or dense networks, shared children, changed schema, missing/deleted items and incomplete source knowledge. A bounded result must explain its scope, not imply a complete impact census.

fields.title: SC-02 — reason about removal
fields.heading: ### SC-02 — reason about removal

### SC-02 — reason about removal

> As an engineer considering removing information, I want to see what relies on it so I can decide how to address those obligations without losing the established history.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** removing, filtering out, disconnecting and superseding are distinguishable; references and unresolved obligations are explained; no silent cascade; established history remains inspectable; users know whether anything was committed.

**Investigate:** actual review/approval authority and the semantics of retirement versus deletion. Do not introduce automatic cascade or organizational approval merely because it would simplify a mockup.

fields.title: SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past

### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past

**Needs:** PN-07, PN-05, PN-08. **Basis:** vision/existing evidence model; detailed reviewer task is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** coverage, freshness, uncertainty and review decision remain separate; original snapshots/rationale remain accessible; the comparison used while drafting is identifiable; a relevant intervening change requires an explicit new assessment rather than silent token adoption; acceptance does not erase drift.

**Exceptions:** missing observations, unrelated edits, relevant later changes, superseded evidence and conflicting reviewer assumptions. Local provenance labels are not authenticated approval authority.

fields.title: 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint
fields.heading: ## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint
fields.excerpt:
## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint

> As an engineer changing an important specification, I want to understand where the value comes from and where it is used so I can assess the consequences without forcing every requirement into a formal model.

**Needs:** PN-06, PN-02, PN-05. **Basis:** UR-5; representation and computation are HY.

**Toy scenario:** an overall timing limit is 100 ms, with explicitly declared 60 ms and 40 ms allocations. Propose changing the total to 80 ms. These are not medical specifications. Any arithmetic requires explicit combination and overhead assumptions.

**Candidate acceptance examples:**

- Free-text-only requirements remain authorable and reviewable.
- If a value is deliberately shared, its confirmed consumers are identifiable; an unrelated identical number is not automatically coupled.
- An explicitly modeled calculation may report a result/violation under its declared assumptions, with units and explanation.
- A parent limit change exposes the allocation question but does not silently proportionally scale or rewrite children.
- A child allocation change can raise a feasibility question for the parent without rewriting the parent's intent.
- Missing derivation knowledge is not represented as a satisfied constraint or no impact.
- Declared constraints, possible engineering impact and review decisions are distinguishable.

**Alternatives to test:** ordinary prose with annotated values, optional named typed values, linked value references, and human-authored derivation explanations. A general formula language or extraction engine is not assumed.

**Additional cases:** inconsistent units, rounding, tolerances, ranges, conditions, repeated values, independent choices and removal of a referenced value. Replace the toy example with one real artifact before specifying storage or arithmetic behavior.

**Candidate acceptance:** context/selection and save status are understandable; switching level or representation does not silently discard drafts; a failed read cannot authorize editing stale information as if current; object/schema conflicts preserve the attempt; historical inspection does not masquerade as editing current state.

**Investigate:** autosave versus explicit save, reopening after shutdown, undo, and what should be retained across sessions. Prototype and actual repository safety capabilities may differ; label unsupported recovery behavior honestly.

fields.title: PN-07 — Judge evidence and record a defensible decision
fields.heading: ### PN-07 — Judge evidence and record a defensible decision

### PN-07 — Judge evidence and record a defensible decision

Inspect relevant inputs/evidence, understand changed or unknown conditions and retain reasoning. **Basis:** VI-1, existing evidence semantics, UR-14; detailed reviewer tasks are HY. Investigate review packages, comparisons, handoffs and authority. A test file, code link and revision-specific result are separate facts; none alone proves need satisfaction. Local review does not imply organizational or medical sign-off.

fields.title: PN-08 — Trust history and recover safely
fields.heading: ### PN-08 — Trust history and recover safely
fields.excerpt:
### PN-08 — Trust history and recover safely

Know what changed/saved, preserve attempted proposals and reconcile interruptions or conflicts without silent loss. Distinguish current, draft and historical information. **Basis:** VI-1, UR-2; preferred recovery is HY. Investigate undo scope, autosave, offline work, interruptions and restoration; history is not undo.

fields.title: PN-09 — Keep orientation while changing working level or representation
fields.heading: ### PN-09 — Keep orientation while changing working level or representation
fields.excerpt:
### PN-09 — Keep orientation while changing working level or representation

Retain scope, selection, drafts and a return path across overview, branch, item and evidence work. **Basis:** UR-1–3/7–8/33/37; VI-1. Investigate persistent state, simultaneous context, keyboard/accessibility, narrow layouts, categorization and direct/contextual actions. Tabs, panels and styling are solutions to evaluate.
